title: 1963 AHSME Problem 32
statement: The dimensions of a rectangle \(R\) are \(a\) and \(b,\) \(a\lt b.\) It is required to obtain a rectangle with dimensions \(x\) and \(y,\) \(x\lt a,\) \(y\lt a,\) so that its perimeter is one-third that of \(R,\) and its area is one-third that of \(R.\) The number of such (different) rectangles is:

solutions.text:
The conditions give \(3(x+y)=a+b\) and \(3xy=ab.\) Dividing yields \[\frac1x+\frac1y=\frac1a+\frac1b.\] But \(x\lt a\) and \(y\lt a\) make the left side greater than \(\frac{2}{a},\) while \(a\lt b\) makes the right side less than \(\frac{2}{a}.\) This is impossible.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Divide the sum equation by the product equation and compare reciprocals using \(x\lt a,\) \(y\lt a,\) and \(a\lt b\)
